subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The Insurance Act, 1938 was enforced with effect from-
answer_html:
Answer: (C) 1 July 1939.

Prior to 1912 there was no insurance law in India and insurance companies were governed by the Indian Companies Act 1882. In 1912 the Indian Life Insurance Companies Act and the Provident Insurance Societies Act were passed to control life insurance only, the first being based on the model of the English Insurance Companies Act of 1909. A Bill introduced in the Legislative Assembly in 1937 emerged as the Insurance Act of 1938, which was enforced since July 1, 1939, and a comprehensive amendment was made in 1950.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Life insurance business in India was nationalised, and the Life Insurance Corporation of India came into existence, respectively in-
answer_html:
Answer: (A) 1956 and on 1 September 1956.

The life insurance business was nationalized in 1956 and the Life Insurance Corporation of India Act, 1956 was passed, the Corporation coming into existence from September 1, 1956. The Marine Insurance Act of 1963 was enacted to govern marine insurance, and general insurance was nationalised in 1972 by the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: A contract of insurance is a contract uberrimae fidei, which means that-

options.A: the insurer alone must observe utmost good faith, the insured being bound only by the policy
options.B: the insured alone must observe utmost good faith, the insurer being protected by its conditions
options.C: neither party may rescind the contract once the first premium has been received by the insurer
options.D: both parties must observe utmost good faith and disclose every material fact known to them

answer_html:
Answer: (D) both parties must observe utmost good faith and disclose every material fact known to them.

A contract of insurance is a contract of utmost good faith, and both the parties to the contract are required to observe utmost good faith and to disclose every material fact known to them. There is no difference between a contract of insurance and any other contract except for this requirement of utmost good faith. Where representations are made an integral part of the contract they become warranties, and the policy is avoidable if they are untrue even if the loss does not arise from the fact concealed or misrepresented.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Which of the following is NOT a contract of indemnity?

options.A: A policy of motor insurance covering damage to a commercial vehicle
options.B: A policy of life insurance or of personal accident insurance
options.C: A policy of fire insurance covering the premises of a factory
options.D: A policy of marine insurance covering a cargo shipped by sea

answer_html:
Answer: (B) A policy of life insurance or of personal accident insurance.

Most kinds of insurance policies other than life and personal accident insurance are contracts of indemnity. Under a contract of indemnity the insured cannot recover more than the actual loss proved, even where that loss is within the maximum limit fixed by the policy. The amount of indemnity is limited by proof of the injury or loss, by the amount specified in the policy, by the requirement of proximate cause, and by the market value of the property.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Insurable interest must be present-

options.A: at both times for a life policy, at the time of taking the policy for fire and motor accident, and at both times for marine
options.B: at the time of the loss in every case, the position at the time of taking the policy being immaterial in all classes
options.C: at the time of taking the policy in every case, the position at the time of the loss being immaterial in all classes
options.D: at the time of taking a life policy, at both times for fire and motor accident, and not at the time of taking a marine policy

answer_html:
Answer: (D) at the time of taking a life policy, at both times for fire and motor accident, and not at the time of taking a marine policy.

In the case of life insurance and personal accident insurance it is sufficient if the insurable interest is present at the time of taking the policy. In the case of fire and motor accident insurance the insurable interest has to be present both at the time of taking the policy and at the time of the accident. In the case of marine insurance there need not be any insurable interest at the time of taking the policy. Where insurable interest is absent the policy amounts to a wager and is void.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The maxim causa proxima non remota spectatur means that the proximate and not the remote cause shall be taken as the cause of loss. The burden of proving that the loss occurred on account of the proximate cause lies on-
answer_html:
Answer: (C) the insured.

The doctrine of proximate cause requires that the proximate and not the remote cause shall be taken as the cause of the loss, and the burden of proof that the loss occurred on account of the proximate cause lies on the insured. Indemnity is available only for losses arising from a proximate cause covered by the policy.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Under Section 42 of the Insurance Act, 1938, a person may act as an insurance agent for-

options.A: any number of insurers, provided the agent discloses the fact of multiple agencies to each of them
options.B: one life insurer, one general insurer, one health insurer and one of each of the other mono-line insurers
options.C: any number of life insurers, but for only one general insurer and one health insurer at any given time
options.D: one insurer only, whatever the class of insurance business which that insurer may be carrying on

answer_html:
Answer: (B) one life insurer, one general insurer, one health insurer and one of each of the other mono-line insurers.

No person shall act as an insurance agent for more than one life insurer, one general insurer, one health insurer and one of each of the other mono-line insurers, and the insurer must ensure that no conflict of interest is allowed to arise for any agent representing two or more insurers. No insurer may appoint any principal agent, chief agent or special agent, multilevel marketing is prohibited, and an insurance agent or intermediary is not eligible to be or remain a director in an insurance company without the permission of the Authority.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act, 1938, a policy of life insurance shall not be called in question on any ground whatsoever after the expiry of-

options.A: three years from the date of the policy
options.B: two years from the date of the policy
options.C: five years from the date of the policy
options.D: one year from the date of the policy

answer_html:
Answer: (A) three years from the date of the policy.

Section 45 bears the heading that a policy is not to be called in question after three years, and provides that no policy of life insurance shall be called in question on any ground whatsoever after the expiry of 3 years from the date of the policy. Where an insurer does repudiate within that period it must communicate in writing to the insured, or to the legal representatives, nominees or assignees, the grounds and the materials on which the decision is based.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
case_facts_html:
Godavari Health Insurance Limited is a company limited by shares, formed and registered under the Companies Act, 2013 as a public company, which proposes to be registered as an Indian insurance company to carry on health insurance business exclusively. Its paid-up equity capital is ₹120 crore.

A group company, Godavari Re Limited, proposes at the same time to be registered to carry on re-insurance business in India.

The Board of Godavari Health Insurance Limited wishes to know the capital it must have, the excess of assets over liabilities it must maintain at all times, and what follows if that excess is not maintained.
question_html: Refer to the case scenario. The minimum paid-up equity capital which Godavari Health Insurance Limited must have under Section 6 is-

options.A: ₹150 crore, which its capital of ₹120 crore does not satisfy
options.B: ₹50 crore, which its capital of ₹120 crore comfortably satisfies
options.C: ₹100 crore, which its capital of ₹120 crore satisfies
options.D: ₹200 crore, which its capital of ₹120 crore does not satisfy

answer_html:
Answer: (C) ₹100 crore, which its capital of ₹120 crore satisfies.

Section 6 fixes the minimum paid-up capital requirement at ₹100 crore for an insurer carrying on life insurance or general insurance business, at ₹100 crore for health insurance business, and at ₹200 crore for re-insurance business. The company proposes to carry on health insurance business, so ₹100 crore is the requirement, and its capital of ₹120 crore exceeds it.

Godavari Health Insurance Limited is a company limited by shares, formed and registered under the Companies Act, 2013 as a public company, which proposes to be registered as an Indian insurance company to carry on health insurance business exclusively. Its paid-up equity capital is ₹120 crore.

A group company, Godavari Re Limited, proposes at the same time to be registered to carry on re-insurance business in India.

The Board of Godavari Health Insurance Limited wishes to know the capital it must have, the excess of assets over liabilities it must maintain at all times, and what follows if that excess is not maintained.
question_html: Refer to the case scenario. The minimum paid-up equity capital which Godavari Re Limited must have to carry on re-insurance business is-
answer_html:
Answer: (B) ₹200 crore.

The minimum paid-up capital prescribed by Section 6 for an insurer carrying on re-insurance business in India is ₹200 crore, as against ₹100 crore for life, general or health insurance business. The capital must consist of equity shares each having a single face value, voting rights are restricted to equity shares, and the paid-up amount must be the same for all shares except during a period not exceeding one year allowed for payment of calls.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
case_facts_html:
Godavari Health Insurance Limited is a company limited by shares, formed and registered under the Companies Act, 2013 as a public company, which proposes to be registered as an Indian insurance company to carry on health insurance business exclusively. Its paid-up equity capital is ₹120 crore.

A group company, Godavari Re Limited, proposes at the same time to be registered to carry on re-insurance business in India.

The Board of Godavari Health Insurance Limited wishes to know the capital it must have, the excess of assets over liabilities it must maintain at all times, and what follows if that excess is not maintained.
question_html: Refer to the case scenario. The excess of the value of assets over the amount of liabilities which Godavari Health Insurance Limited must maintain at all times is-

options.A: ₹60 crore, being fifty per cent of the paid-up capital actually subscribed
options.B: ₹100 crore, being the whole of the minimum capital stated in Section 6
options.C: ₹25 crore, being twenty-five per cent of the minimum capital so stated
options.D: ₹50 crore, being fifty per cent of the minimum capital stated in Section 6

answer_html:
Answer: (D) ₹50 crore, being fifty per cent of the minimum capital stated in Section 6.

Every insurer and re-insurer shall at all times maintain an excess of the value of assets over the amount of liabilities of not less than fifty per cent of the amount of minimum capital as stated under Section 6. For health insurance business the minimum capital is ₹100 crore, so the required excess is ₹50 crore. The measure is the statutory minimum capital, not the capital actually subscribed.

question_html: Refer to the case scenario. An insurer which does not maintain the required excess of assets over liabilities-

options.A: shall be required to transfer its business to another insurer under a scheme approved by the Authority
options.B: shall be deemed to be insolvent and may be wound up by the court on an application made by the Authority
options.C: shall be deemed to be insolvent and shall stand dissolved without any order of any court being required
options.D: shall have its certificate of registration cancelled by the Central Government without any further enquiry

answer_html:
Answer: (B) shall be deemed to be insolvent and may be wound up by the court on an application made by the Authority.

An insurer which does not comply with the requirement shall be deemed to be insolvent and may be wound up by the court on an application made by the Authority. The Authority may also specify a level of solvency margin known as the control level of solvency, on the breach of which it acts, without prejudice to the taking of any other remedial measures as it deems fit.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority was established by the Government of India in the year-
answer_html:
Answer: (A) 1999.

The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority was established in the year 1999 by the Indian Government. Its objectives are to protect the interests of holders of insurance policies, to regulate, promote and ensure the orderly growth of the industry, and to deal with matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. Based on the report of the Malhotra Committee, the insurance market in India was opened up for the private sector in 2000.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The Authority consists of a Chairperson together with-

options.A: a maximum of three whole-time members and a maximum of six part-time members
options.B: a maximum of six whole-time members and a maximum of three part-time members
options.C: a maximum of five whole-time members and a maximum of four part-time members
options.D: a maximum of four whole-time members and a maximum of five part-time members

answer_html:
Answer: (C) a maximum of five whole-time members and a maximum of four part-time members.

The Authority is appointed by the Central Government by notification and is in the nature of a body corporate. It consists of a Chairman, a maximum of five whole-time members and a maximum of four part-time members, making ten in all, appointed depending upon their expertise and experience in fields such as insurance, law, economics and accountancy. The head office of the Authority is to be decided by the Central Government.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The Chairperson of the Authority holds office for a term of-

options.A: three years or until he attains the age of sixty-two years, and is not eligible for re-appointment
options.B: five years or until he attains the age of sixty-two years, and is not eligible for re-appointment
options.C: six years or until he attains the age of seventy years, and is eligible for one re-appointment
options.D: five years or until he attains the age of sixty-five years, and is eligible for re-appointment

answer_html:
Answer: (D) five years or until he attains the age of sixty-five years, and is eligible for re-appointment.

The Chairperson holds office for a term of five years until he reaches sixty-five years of age, and is eligible for re-appointment. A whole-time member can hold office up to sixty-two years of age. A member may relinquish his membership by giving three months' prior notice to the Central Government.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Under Section 6 of the Act, a member may be removed from office where he-

options.A: becomes insolvent or insane, refuses to act on a direction of the Central Government, or accepts employment with an insurer during his term of office with the Authority
options.B: becomes insolvent or insane, is convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude, establishes an illegal financial interest in the Authority, or acts contrary to the public interest
options.C: becomes insolvent or insane, is convicted of any offence whatsoever, absents himself from three consecutive meetings, or is censured by the Central Government in that behalf
options.D: becomes insolvent, attains the age of sixty years, is convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude, or fails to relinquish an interest in an insurance company on appointment

answer_html:
Answer: (B) becomes insolvent or insane, is convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude, establishes an illegal financial interest in the Authority, or acts contrary to the public interest.

Section 6 permits removal where the member has become insolvent or insane, has been convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude, has illegally established a financial interest in the Authority, or has acted contrary to the public interest. The Chairperson and the whole-time members are also subject to a bar of two years on holding office under the Central Government, a State Government or any insurance sector entity.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Fund is constituted under Section 16 of the Act, and-

options.A: is applied to the settlement of claims of policyholders whose insurers have been wound up, and is audited by an auditor appointed by the Central Government for the purpose
options.B: is applied to the salaries and allowances of members, officers and employees alone, and is audited by an auditor appointed by the Authority from a panel maintained by it
options.C: is applied to the other legitimate expenses of the Authority alone, and is audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General at the expense of the Central Government
options.D: is applied to the salaries and allowances of members, officers and employees and to the other legitimate expenses of the Authority, and is audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General

answer_html:
Answer: (D) is applied to the salaries and allowances of members, officers and employees and to the other legitimate expenses of the Authority, and is audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General.

The Fund is called the IRDA of India Fund. It is credited with Government grants, fees and charges, with the prescribed percentage of premium income received from insurers, and with money received from other sources specified by the Central Government. It is applied to meeting the salaries and allowances of the members, officers and employees of the Authority and its other legitimate expenses. The accounts are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General, the expenditure for the audit being borne by the Authority, and the certified accounts are laid before Parliament.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Where the Authority persistently defaults in complying with a direction of the Central Government, or where the public interest so requires, the Central Government may-

options.A: supersede the Authority for a period of not more than six months by notification, appointing a person as Controller of Insurance
options.B: supersede the Authority for a period of not more than twelve months by notification, appointing a Chairperson in place of the existing one
options.C: dissolve the Authority by notification and transfer its functions to the Securities and Exchange Board of India for the interim period
options.D: suspend the whole-time members for a period of not more than six months, the part-time members continuing to hold office

answer_html:
Answer: (A) supersede the Authority for a period of not more than six months by notification, appointing a person as Controller of Insurance.

The Authority is bound by the action of the Central Government on policy matters, retaining independence on technical and administrative matters. Where there is persistent default in complying with directions of the Central Government, or where the public interest requires it, the Central Government may supersede the Authority for not more than six months by notification and appoint a person as Controller of Insurance. The Central Government also constitutes the Authority and appoints the Chairperson and other members.
